full_judgment:
Abdul Bari Sarker J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by Mr. Md. Golam Maola, Special Tribunal Judge, Moulvibazar in Special Powers Act Case No. 43 of 1988.

 6. Mr. AKM Faiz, the learned Advocate for the appellant has taken us to the facts of the case. He submits that the conviction of the appellant is illegal on the face of it and there is no iota of evidence to sustain the conviction. He submits that the facts of the case does not warrant a conviction under section 4(c) of the Cruelty to Women Ordinance. The contention of the learned Advocate seems to be correct, because section 4(c) of the Cruelty to Women Ordinance runs as follows: 

 7. In the present case there is no allegation whatsoever of any abduction of the alleged victim PW 1 either in the FIR or in her deposition in Court which runs as follows: 

 9. Mr. M Shamsul Alam, the learned Deputy Attorney-General concedes that he is unable to support the impugned judgment and conviction of the appellant under section 4(c) of the Cruelty to Women Ordinance in view of the above facts and circumstances of the case. He however submits that the case should be sent back on remand for retrial of the appellant after framing charge on proper section of the Penal Code and presumably section 493 BPC. As the accused allegedly had sexual intercourse with PW 1 on promise that he would marry her and thereby the victim gave birth to a child. We are of opinion that the facts of the present case as disclosed above does not come within the mischief of section 493 BPC which runs as follows : 

 10. In the present case there is allegation that the accused by deceit caused PW 1 to believe that she is lawfully married to him before he had sexual intercourse with her and she engaged in sexual intercourse with the appellant on the belief that she was lawfully married to him. In the FIR it is stated that on 16.5.85 the appellant compromised to marry the PW 1 but as she did not believe he swore by taking the holy Quaran in hands in the language of the FIR. 

 11. From the above it is clear that PW 1 would know that there was no marriage between her and the accused and accused only compromised to marry her on some future date. She had no reason to believe that she is not lawfully married to him (the appellant)". Thus the statement made in the FIR Ext. 1 does not come within the mischief of offence punishable under section 493 BPC. 

 13. Thus the statement made in Court also does not come within the mischief of an offence punishable under section 493 BPC. 14. So far the allegation of rape, an offence under Section 376 BPC is concerned, it is evident that the statement made by PW 1 in the FIR or in Court does not come within the mischief of rape defined under section 375 and made punishable under section 376 BPC as she was a willing party and had sexual intercourse with the appellant quite willingly for a long time and got a child by him. From the above, it is clear that no useful purpose will be served by sending the case on remand as PW 1 had voluntarily engaged in sexual intercourse with the appellant and the offence does not come within the mischief of any of the sections 376 or 493 BPC or section 4(c) of the Cruelty to Women Ordinance, 1983.
